works.title: Ultrathin b ‐Oriented Co‐Gallate MOF Membranes for Lithium Recovery: Precise Ion Sieving via Geometry‐Confined Dehydration
institutions: Henan University of Science and Technology
Faculty of Arts and Sciences Beijing Normal University Zhuhai China
Center for Advanced Materials Research Advanced Institute of Natural Sciences Beijing Normal University Zhuhai China
College of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering Henan University of Science and Technology Luoyang China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Selective K + over Li + separation is indispensable for lithium recovery from salt‐lake brines, whereas simultaneous high‐efficiency separation of K + from interfering Na + and Mg 2+ cations remains challenging for pristine MOF membranes. Herein, an ultrathin b ‐oriented Co‐gallate MOF membrane is fabricated using a gas–liquid interfacial soft‐template approach. The membrane possesses 3D interconnected zigzag subnanochannels (≈3.7 Å) that impose geometry‐confined ion dehydration, hindering the transport of Li + , Na + , and Mg 2+ far more significantly than K + , as corroborated by molecular dynamics simulations. Under a concentration gradient driving force, the u b ‐CoG membrane achieves a prominent K + /Li + selectivity of 13.5, as well as excellent K + /Na + and K + /Mg 2+ sieving capability. The recorded K + /Li + selectivity stands as the highest value among MOF ion‐sieving membranes. This interfacial orientation strategy provides a promising pathway to advanced ion‐sieving membranes for multicomponent industrial brine lithium extraction.

works.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) unlock opportunities to unite rapid mass transport with molecular-level sieving through membranes. However, achieving long-range crystallographic order within these membranes remains a central challenge that limits their separation precision. Here, we report a monomer-driven strategy for the ambient-condition fabrication of COF polycrystalline membranes featuring definite lattice order and polyhedral textures, reminiscent of benchmark metal-organic framework counterparts. Using a rigid, π-conjugated pyrene-centered tetraamine, we enable nonepitaxial intergrowth of faceted COF crystals on a porous support, yielding a 350-nanometer-thick membrane with a record-high Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 2121 square meters per gram among COF separation membranes of comparable pore size. The resulting COF membrane preserves its crystallographic order and polyhedral texture even after 1 month of solvent exposure while uniquely combining increased surface stiffness with high tensile ductility. Notably, we demonstrate its superior liquid-phase molecular selectivity, outperforming COF analogs with considerably smaller pore apertures, and elucidate an unambiguous correlation between crystallographic order and permselectivity. This work positions crystallographic ordering as a guiding principle for COF membranes, opening more possibilities at the intersection of framework materials and separation technologies.

works.title: Interface‐Induced Growth of Macroscopic, Free‐Standing, and Flexible Monolithic Pure MOF Membrane With Adaptive Porosity
institutions: Hefei National Center for Physical Sciences at Nanoscale
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Membrane‐based separation technologies have emerged as energy‐efficient and environmentally sustainable alternatives to traditional industrial separation processes. However, the development of high‐performance separation membranes faces fundamental material challenges, as amorphous polymeric materials typically exhibit poorly controlled pore size distributions while crystalline porous materials encounter intrinsic difficulties in forming continuous, defect‐free membranes at the macroscopic scale owing to inevitable crystal boundaries. Despite their exceptional structural tunability and separation potential, MOF membranes face fundamental challenges in defect‐free fabrication due to intrinsic crystallinity constraints. Integrating the structural precision of crystalline MOFs with the adaptivity of polymers, we successfully fabricated a macroscopic, free‐standing, and flexible monolithic pure MOF membrane through interface‐induced coordination of Co 2+ with the flexible multidentate amino acid ligand 2,6‐diaminopimelic acid (DAP). The flexible alkyl‐chain backbone suppresses long‐range crystallization and reduces interfacial strain during continuous membrane growth. Locally defined Co–amino‐acid coordination units preserve a framework scaffold, while conformationally flexible alkyl segments impart guest‐responsive latent free volume. The flexible Co‐DAP membrane exhibits guest‐responsive dynamic porosity, in which hydration generates water‐accessible transport pathways that regulate hydrated‐state molecular and ionic transport, enabling osmotically driven water/ion separation through coupled transport and interfacial electrostatic effects under conditions relevant to forward osmosis.

works.title: Recent Advances in the Preparation, Structural Modulation, and Applications of Metal–Organic Framework (MOF) Membrane Materials in the Field of Separation
institutions: Zhejiang University of Science and Technology
College of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering Qiqihar University Qiqihar China
Heilongjiang Provincial Key Laboratory of Polymeric Composition College of Materials Science and Engineering Qiqihar University Qiqihar China
School of Environmental and Nature Resources Zhejiang University of Science and Technology Hangzhou China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal–organic framework (MOF) membranes are a novel class of composite membranes. They use crystalline porous MOF materials as separation layers or functional fillers. Because of their well‐ordered and tunable pore structures and highly controllable chemical environments, MOF membranes show broad application prospects in gas separation, pervaporation, nanofiltration, ion sieving, and water treatment. This paper systematically reviews the fundamental characteristics, primary configurations, separation mechanisms, preparation methods, and structural regulation strategies of MOF membranes. It also covers their application progress in typical separation fields. First, based on the composition and structural features of MOFs, we summarize the advantages and limitations of four configurations: polycrystalline MOF membranes, mixed matrix membranes, two‐dimensional (2D) MOF layered membranes, and MOF glass membranes. The separation mechanism is then elaborated, which relies on the synergy between pore‐size sieving and chemical interactions. Second, we compare in detail the principles, applicable systems, and technical bottlenecks of various preparation methods. These include in situ growth, secondary growth, interface‐assisted growth, counter‐diffusion, vapor‐assisted conversion, and electrochemical deposition. On this basis, we systematically summarize the structural regulation strategies of MOF membranes from six aspects: crystal orientation, membrane thickness, defect engineering, intra‐pore chemical environment, interface engineering, and stability enhancement. Their influence on separation performance is also discussed. We emphasize the necessity of multi‐scale synergistic regulation. Furthermore, we present the latest research progress on MOF membranes for gas separation, pervaporation, nanofiltration, organic solvent nanofiltration, ion sieving, resource recovery, water treatment, and oil–water separation. Typical case studies are provided to analyze the structure’s performance relationship. Finally, we summarize the challenges currently faced by MOF membranes and present corresponding prospects. This paper aims to provide a systematic reference for the rational design and engineering application of MOF separation membranes.

works.title: Confined Growth of MOFs into Angstrom-Scale Defect-Free Membranes for Precise Molecular Separation
works.abstract: Conspectus Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), featuring ordered nanochannels and versatile pore chemistry, have emerged as promising materials for developing next-generation separation membranes. MOF-based membranes are typically synthesized either by the intergrowth of crystals to form polycrystalline membranes or by incorporating crystals into polymers to form mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs). During the membrane formation processes, multiscale defects─ranging from microscale intercrystalline cracks and nanoscale interfacial gaps to angstrom-scale lattice defects─are prone to arise. These undesirable defects compromise the membrane structural integrity and molecular transport properties, thus impairing the separation efficiency and impeding the implementation of MOF-based membranes for precise molecular separation. In this Account, we present our group’s efforts to construct defect-free molecular sieving membranes based on the “confined growth of MOFs”. We first establish MOF design and selection principles by correlating molecular transport mechanisms with framework characteristics. We then demonstrate how confined growth enables the elimination of multiscale defects in both polycrystalline membranes and MMMs. For polycrystalline membranes, the elimination of angstrom-scale lattice defects has been a long-standing challenge. To address this, we proposed a high-probability theoretical coordination strategy that creates sufficient chemical potential to overcome the steric hindrance that occurs when connecting ligands to metal clusters. By further regulating the confinement of coordination reactants (e.g., ligands, metal cluster precursor), coordination environment (e.g., solvent, modulator), and coordination space (e.g., pore size, topology), we inhibited the linker-missing and metal cluster-missing defects and restored intrinsic lattice integrity in MOF membranes. This leads to a family of high-connectivity MOF membranes exhibiting outstanding molecular separation performance, not only for gases but also for water/ions and organic mixtures. By employing atomic-level characterizations (e.g., real-space high-resolution transmission electron microscopy) and molecular simulations, we revealed the underlying thermodynamics and kinetic mechanism of defect suppression and confined molecular transport through the lattice aperture. For MMMs, despite the structural integrity achieved in the as-synthesized crystals, incorporating these crystals into polymers remains another grand challenge because this process often introduces multiscale defects resulting from filler aggregation and interfacial incompatibility. Recognizing that the space between MOF fillers and the polymer matrix represents a typical confined environment, we pursued molecular-confined strategies to solve the dispersion and compatibility issues in MMMs. Recently, we proposed a solid-solvent processing strategy to fabricate an ultrathin and highly loaded defect-free MMM for molecular sieving. The polymer serves as a solid solvent, confining MOF nucleation and in situ growth on the polymer chains to avoid crystal aggregation and interfacial defects. This yields a new-generation nanocomposite membrane with MOF crystals as the continuous phase, enabling fast molecular transport through interconnected MOF nanochannels. Notably, this general polymer-confined growth allows for the scalable fabrication of MMMs toward diverse molecular separation applications including hydrogen separation, CO2 capture, and organic azeotropic separations. By integrating machine learning and high-throughput calculations, our group also explored the AI-accelerated design and customized synthesis of MOF-based membranes. We conclude this Account by discussing the remaining limitations, challenges, and opportunities of further exploring angstrom-scale defect-free MOF membranes. We hope that this Account can provide insights in developing next-generation molecularly selective separation membranes toward broad applications and stimulate or deepen interest in multiple disciplines crossing chemistry, materials science, and chemical engineering.

works.title: Interfacial engineering of UiO-66-NH2 nanofillers in TFN membranes for simultaneous salt and boron removal
institutions: King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals
works.abstract: The fabrication of high-performance desalination membranes capable of removing both ionic species and neutral trace contaminants is critical for advancing seawater desalination. Due to their crystalline nature, tunable porosity, and hybrid inorganic-organic composition, metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have shown remarkable potential for selective ion removal while maintaining high water recovery. Hence, in this work, we have synthesized nanosized UiO-66-NH 2 to enhance crystal uniformity and reduce defect density during the nanofiller incorporation in the reverse osmosis (RO) membrane. The core of the current study was to explore the optimal strategy for uniformly incorporating this MOF into the polyamide active layer of thin-film nanocomposite (TFN) membranes. Three distinct interfacial polymerization strategies were employed: TFN-A (aqueous-phase dispersion), TFN-O (organic-phase dispersion), and TFN-I (dip-coating on the support layer). Among the fabricated membranes, TFN-A exhibited the highest water flux (up to ~33.8 LMH at 30 ± 1 bar transmembrane pressure) and superior salt rejection (98.8%) under brackish water conditions (2000 mg L −1 NaCl). The TFN-A also exhibits high desalination performance across a range of NaCl and other divalent salt concentrations. The fabricated membrane also shows tremendous performance during long term test for 48 h and improved antifouling properties. Further, the boron rejection tests using 5 mg L −1 boron demonstrate that TFN-A achieves 87.8% rejection in the absence of competing salts and 81.8% rejection in simulated brackish water (2000 mg L −1 NaCl and 5 mg L −1 boron). Furthermore, this study has explored boron rejection at different pH values of the feed, which reveals that boron rejection increases significantly at alkaline pH, reaching 98.1% for TFN-A at pH 13 due to the conversion of boric acid into large borate ions. Hence, the results of the current study highlighted the role of nanosized MOFs in enhancing interfacial compatibility, overall separation performance, and the rejection of challenging neutral species, such as boron, from saline water.

works.title: Interface‐Induced Growth of Macroscopic, Free‐Standing, and Flexible Monolithic Pure MOF Membrane With Adaptive Porosity
institutions: Hefei National Center for Physical Sciences at Nanoscale
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Membrane‐based separation technologies have emerged as energy‐efficient and environmentally sustainable alternatives to traditional industrial separation processes. However, the development of high‐performance separation membranes faces fundamental material challenges, as amorphous polymeric materials typically exhibit poorly controlled pore size distributions while crystalline porous materials encounter intrinsic difficulties in forming continuous, defect‐free membranes at the macroscopic scale owing to inevitable crystal boundaries. Despite their exceptional structural tunability and separation potential, MOF membranes face fundamental challenges in defect‐free fabrication due to intrinsic crystallinity constraints. Integrating the structural precision of crystalline MOFs with the adaptivity of polymers, we successfully fabricated a macroscopic, free‐standing, and flexible monolithic pure MOF membrane through interface‐induced coordination of Co 2+ with the flexible multidentate amino acid ligand 2,6‐diaminopimelic acid (DAP). The flexible alkyl‐chain backbone suppresses long‐range crystallization and reduces interfacial strain during continuous membrane growth. Locally defined Co–amino‐acid coordination units preserve a framework scaffold, while conformationally flexible alkyl segments impart guest‐responsive latent free volume. The flexible Co‐DAP membrane exhibits guest‐responsive dynamic porosity, in which hydration generates water‐accessible transport pathways that regulate hydrated‐state molecular and ionic transport, enabling osmotically driven water/ion separation through coupled transport and interfacial electrostatic effects under conditions relevant to forward osmosis.

works.title: Molecular Dynamics Insights into Water Flux and Salt Rejection in Nitrogen-Doped Carbon Nanotubes Incorporated with Ag Nanoparticles for Capacitive Deionization
works.abstract: Capacitive deionization (CDI) is an environmentally friendly and energy-efficient method for saline water desalination; however, conventional carbon-based electrodes are often limited by low salt adsorption capacity (SAC). In this study, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were used to investigate the desalination performance of nitrogen-doped carbon nanotube (N-CNT) and silver-encapsulated N-CNT (Ag/N-CNT) electrodes under pressure-driven flow and varying electric field strengths. The results show that water flux is strongly field-dependent in both systems, with Ag/N-CNT exhibiting significantly higher flux due to the presence of Ag nanoparticles. Notably, increasing the electric field enhances salt rejection in N-CNT electrodes but reduces it in Ag/N-CNT. At high electric fields, high water flux promotes severe Na + -Cl − cluster formation in pristine N-CNT. These clusters experience restricted entry into the nanochannels, which hinders ion capture and prevents ions from reaching the pure-water reservoir, thereby increasing salt rejection at the expense of SAC. In contrast, the Ag/N-CNT system mitigates this effect through Ag-induced selective dehydration of Cl − ions. This process disrupts the symmetry of the hydration shells and suppresses ionic cluster nucleation, allowing dispersed, mobile ions to readily enter the nanochannels. This significantly enhances SAC through efficient ion capture, although a portion of the ions permeates into the pure-water reservoir, leading to a decrease in salt rejection. Consequently, an inherent trade-off between high SAC and salt rejection emerges under high-throughput conditions. Despite this trade-off, the superior water flux and enhanced SAC of Ag/N-CNT highlight its potential for high-throughput CDI applications and provide atomistic insights for electrode design.

works.title: Coupling advanced treatments with reactive barrier infiltration for pharmaceutical micropollutants removal in the context of water reuse
institutions: École Nationale Supérieure de Chimie de Montpellier
Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Institut de Recherche pour le Développement
works.abstract: Recharging aquifers with treated wastewater provides multiple benefits for sustainable water management, but micropollutants in effluents can threaten groundwater quality, aquatic ecosystems, and human health. Infiltration-based recharge can improve water quality and remove micropollutants, a performance that can be enhanced by reactive barriers. Advanced treatments such as nanofiltration or ozonation can also achieve high micropollutant abatement. This study evaluated micropollutant removal through reactive barrier infiltration alone and coupled with nanofiltration or ozonation, using three identical lab-scale columns containing a reactive barrier of 70% sand, 25% sawdust, and 5% compost over 37 days. Influent waters were wastewater effluent, ozonated effluent, or nanofiltration permeate. Redox zonation was suggested all columns, with substantial removal of nitrogen species and sulphates, while dissolved organic carbon slightly increased in outlets. Positively charged micropollutants metoprolol and venlafaxine were highly removed (>90%), whereas neutral and negatively charged compounds showed variable behaviours. Biodegradation may have contributed to the removal of sulfamethoxazole (∼60%), irbesartan (∼30%), and oxazepam (<20%), while fluconazole, carbamazepine, and diclofenac were largely refractory. Microbiological indicators confirmed effective pathogen removal in all scenarios. Coupling reactive barrier infiltration with nanofiltration or ozonation improved overall micropollutants removal: at least 5 of 8 micropollutants were removed over 80%, and 7 were removed over 50%. Only fluconazole and carbamazepine remained refractory to ozonation-reactive barrier and nanofiltration-reactive barrier coupling, respectively. These results demonstrate that combining low-cost infiltration with advanced treatments can substantially enhance micropollutant removal, supporting safe water reuse for managed aquifer recharge.
